liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **New Potato Caboose** (4 reviews): Phil takes a fine lead after the weak verses, and Jerry answers with amazing jamming; A mostly jammy version with fewer vocals [7][11][12][17]
- **Dupree's Diamond Blues** (1 review, 3 other sources): Pigpen plays harmonica on Dupree's Diamond Blues; Pigpen plays harmonica on Dupree's [1][2][3][14]
- **Dark Star** (2 reviews): A false start enters the second verse; a broken string possibly prevented a first 20-minute version, running 19:45; A rather mellow version exploring new territory, found to be the most enjoyable part [7][16]
- **Cryptical Envelopment** (1 review): The long Cryptical Envelopment after a strong Other One is liked [11]
- **Turn on Your Lovelight** (1 review): Lovelight seems to cut in around the middle [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **End of Set One**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [19]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Dupree's Diamond Blues, Doin' That Rag [19]

## The recordings

- **gd69-01-24.sbd.kaplan.7922.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 11 songs; 84 min; rated 3.64/5 by 14 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound quality is excellent, with instruments and vocals clear and well placed; Early 16-track recording caused predictable audio problems, which were fixed fairly quickly; Sound quality is a standard, decent soundboard [9][10][13][16]
- **gd1969-01-24.sbd.kaplan.2244.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 8 songs; 41 min; rated 3.75/5 by 4 [3]
- **gd1969-01-24.sbd.miller.109640.flac16**: soundboard; 7 songs; 84 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [4]. Said about its sound: There are serious mix problems at the start of the show, and the beginning of Lovelight is cut [4]
- **gd1969-01-24.sbd.kaplan.2370.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 8 songs; 41 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [2]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: Sons of Champlin [1]
- Management pulled the power plug halfway through Lovelight, ending the show on a down note [7]
- The Lovelight ended with an intentional power failure, perhaps inspiring the Alligator lyric about burning down the Fillmore and gassing the Avalon [9]
- The Avalon required bands to play sets of an hour or less; this may be the complete first set [1]
- An announcement at the start of disc two says the Dead are leaving the stage, Sons of Champlin are introduced, and the Dead will return [1]
- The Avalon insisted on sets of an hour or less; this may be the full first set [2]
- The Avalon insisted on sets of an hour or less; this may be the full first set [3]
- Sons of Champlin and Initial Shock were also on the bill [4]
- This Dark Star is far weaker than the one on 2/27/69 [9]
- It does not blow the roof off like some other shows from the period [12]
- The other two January Avalon nights, especially the 25th, are much better than this one [16]
- The rest of the show is less impressive than the other Avalon shows [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-01-24.sbd.kaplan.7922.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Seth Kaplan; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: The late January 1969 Avalon shows are cited in 'A Long Strange Trip' as the first live 16-track recordings, made for Live/Dead [10]
- **gd1969-01-24.sbd.kaplan.2244.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Extraction and shortening by Seth Kaplan; source: MSR>C>DAT>CD [3]. Also: Some tracks were not properly sector aligned; fixed with shntool, with new md5 checksum files issued 12/7/00 [3]
- **gd1969-01-24.sbd.miller.109640.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (44.1k) [4]. Also: Transferred from DATs lent by Rob Eaton [4]
- **gd1969-01-24.sbd.kaplan.2370.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Extraction and shortening by Seth Kaplan; source: SBD : MR>C>DAT>CD [2]
